conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad to meet you. I’m a clinician who specializes in the emotional well-being of new mothers, and I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. Today we’ll be using a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—or EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 gentle questions about your mood and thoughts over the past seven days. There are no right or wrong answers; whatever you share stays between us unless safety is a concern, and my only goal is to make sure you feel heard and supported. Ready to begin?

Let’s start with the first question:  
In the past week, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you smile, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

Honestly? Most things feel pretty flat. I can still get a flicker of pleasure when my little guy gives me a gummy grin, but even that feels dimmer—like someone turned the volume down on happiness. Before he was born, a cup of coffee and a podcast used to feel like a treat; now I drink it just to stay awake and hardly taste it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… I’ve chuckled once or twice when my husband made a dumb joke about diapers, but it felt forced, like I was going through the motions. Most of the time I just feel too tired or heavy inside to find anything funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much. I used to get excited about little stuff—like a walk to the coffee shop or a phone call with my best friend—but now even planning those things feels like a chore. I still go through the motions because I know I *should*, but the spark isn’t really there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If he spits up more than usual, I immediately think it’s because I ate something “wrong.” When he wouldn’t settle last night, I kept replaying every little choice—was the room too warm, did I wait too long between feeds, am I just not reading his cues? My head keeps telling me a “good mom” would handle it better, even when my husband says stuff just happens with babies.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. My mind keeps spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby—what if he stops breathing in his sleep, what if I drop him, what if there’s something wrong and I don’t notice in time. Nothing’s actually happened, but the thoughts just pop up and loop until I feel tight in my chest. Sometimes I can distract myself, but it’s like the worry is always humming in the background.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… it’s happened a few times. All of a sudden my heart starts racing and I feel like I can’t catch my breath, even though nothing’s happening. The other night I was just rocking him in the dim light and out of nowhere I felt this wave of terror—like something awful was about to happen. It passed after a minute, but it left me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days feel like I’m barely treading water. I’ll be feeding him and notice the laundry pile or dishes and think, “I’ll never get through it.” Sometimes my chest gets tight and I just want to hide, but I can’t—he needs me—so I push through. I haven’t had anything to drink or take; I just keep going, even when it feels overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my brain won’t shut off—keeps replaying everything I think I did wrong that day or might mess up tomorrow. It takes me almost an hour to drift off, and then I wake up at like two and four a.m. with my heart pounding, sure I heard him cry even when the monitor’s quiet. By morning I’m more tired than when I went to bed.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel that way most of the day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud hanging over me. I’ll be holding the baby and tears just well up for no clear reason. I try to smile so my older daughter doesn’t worry, but inside I feel heavy and hollow.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I just sat on the couch with him asleep on my chest and started sobbing. Nothing specific triggered it—I just felt overwhelmed and so, so low. The tears came and I couldn’t stop them for a while.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…I’ve had a couple of quick flashes this week, like “what if I just disappeared,” but they’re momentary and I shake them off right away. I’ve never made a plan or wanted to act on it—I couldn’t leave my kids—but yeah, the thought has popped in.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary

Patient: Postpartum mother, ≤12 wks post-delivery (per clinical context)

Symptoms endorsed
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness (Q1-2, 8-9)
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)
- Daily, intrusive "what-if" worries; nocturnal panic episodes (Q4-5)
- Overwhelmed, "treading water," physical tension (Q6)
- Initial & middle insomnia driven by ruminative worry (Q7)
- Passive, fleeting self-harm ideation without intent or plan (Q10)

Pattern
All 10 items indicate clinically significant distress; highest severity on mood, anxiety, and coping items. No psychotic content or substance use noted.

Risk flags
- Depressed mood + anhedonia most days
- Anxiety/panic "humming in background," nocturnal surges
- Self-blame, perceived maternal inadequacy
- Passive suicidal ideation this week (safety issue)

Screening impression
Scores and narrative suggest high likelihood of major postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; passive SI present. Recommend immediate formal evaluation (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS) and safety assessment; consider expedited referral to perinatal mental health specialty or crisis service if SI escalates.
